description: Students at the French School of Bahrain interested in NASA and programming.
summary: AMWS (Astronaut Mission Wrist System) is a simulated wrist-worn health and life-support monitor for astronauts on Moon and Mars surface missions. It gathers health indicators (heart rate, SpO2, respiration, body temperature, CO2 exposure, radiation dose) and suit data, classifies each against NASA-style Caution, Warning and Emergency levels, and turns them into one decision: Return Margin, the minutes of oxygen, power, CO2 scrubbing and cooling that would remain after walking back to the habitat. The model is based on NASA's 10 km Walkback Test. With Earth up to 22 minutes away on Mars, astronauts must evaluate and act on their own health status. Every value is either sourced to a NASA document or labelled ASSUMED. It is a concept, not a medical device.
details:
What it does: AMWS shows a crew member their physiological and environmental status and one hero number, Return Margin, with the limiting resource named. Alerts follow NASA's Emergency/Warning/Caution/Advisory hierarchy. Automatic emergency mode triggers only on three time-critical conditions (rapid pressure loss, toxic CO2, critically low O2). Comms show real light-time delay, and emergency procedures live on the wrist (illustrative, not flight-certified).

How it works: a metabolic-rate model drives O2, CO2 scrubbing, cooling and battery use. Return Margin uses the walkback pace and burn rate from NASA's Walkback Test, not the current workload. Environment profiles (Earth orbit, Moon, Mars, custom) change gravity, distance and delay, radiation and walking cost. Unsourced values are marked ASSUMED.

Benefits and intended impact: one glanceable, glove-operable decision aid that works offline under communication delay, helping astronauts evaluate and act on their own health when Earth cannot answer in time.

Honesty and limits: we removed readiness, stress, fatigue and ECG displays because we found no validated NASA model behind them. Data is simulated. Vital-sign alarm limits, alert bands and Mars walking pace are ASSUMED. The walkback figures come from a preliminary 2007 treadmill study. Immune, bone and behavioral health are not covered. Automated tests check the simulation, alerts, config source tags, demo run and environments.

Tools: HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, Node test scripts, GitHub, Vercel. No external libraries.

How to evaluate in 2 minutes: open https://amws.vercel.app and press RUN 60 s DEMO (or add ?demo=1). No login needed. Source code: https://github.com/naeldavid/AMWS_nasa-spaceapps-project/

Use of Super Intelligence (SI): code, tests and documentation were developed with SI assistance (Claude by Anthropic and the Kiro coding agent), and Claude was also used for literature search and review of sources. The team set the research direction, made the design decisions, checked claims against NASA sources, and tested the result. This is also stated in the README, the code headers and the page metadata. No SI-generated images or NASA branding are used.
